THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants are in appeal challenging the exoneration of liability and also seeking for enhancement of compensation for the death of Savithramm, 32 years old.
2. The Tribunal has exonerated the insurer on the ground of violation of policy and conditions.
In the light of settled law that in cases of breach of policy conditions the insurer has to pay the compensation and recover the same, the exoneration of liability of the insurer cannot be sustained.
It is held that the insurer is liable to pay the compensation and thereafter proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

3. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded the following sums :
 Sl.

4. In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.8,000/- per month.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
5.
Since the deceased was aged 32 years and was self- employed, 40% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.12,600/-.
If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.8,400/-.
6. The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.8,400/-.
7. As the deceased was aged 32 years, a multiplier of '16' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.16,12,800/- (Rs.8,400/- x 12 x '16') towards 'loss of dependency'.
8.

The claimants being husband, daughter and mother- in-law, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' i.e., in all Rs.1,32,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the 'conventional heads'.
9. Further, as per the medical bills, the claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.1,10,340/- towards 'medical expenses'.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.18,88,140/- as against Rs.13,39,300/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

13. On deposit, Rs.14,00,000/- shall be deposited in the name of appellant No.2 - minor in any Nationalised Bank till she attains the age of majority with liberty to appellant No.1 (father) to withdraw the interest accrued thereon and remaining amount along with interest shall be released equally to appellant No.1 and appellant No.3 by way of Account Payee cheque with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
14. However, the claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 412 days.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
